rationale: The natural-timing probe ran (CheckRun c839d00a425a4b75b09fbfb353fc4fc8, exit 0) and returned the no-fall branch: 792 fast-path deliveries, all successful, 792 term samples taken right after them, zero falls, and a term that climbed monotonically to 2390 in memory and in the stable store. That is the honest and expected outcome for a window a couple of instructions wide, and it bounds rather than refutes the finding. What it says is that under this schedule the interleaving did not happen once in 792 delivery opportunities, so the natural hit probability per delivery is small - on the order of a fraction of a percent at most, which is consistent with the window being microseconds against a delivery every few milliseconds - and it says nothing about whether a schedule that lands deliveries more densely on election starts would do better, nor about clusters where campaigns last longer. I record the observation with its operands, state the resulting bound and the caveat that my deliveries were bursty rather than uniformly distributed in time so the per-delivery figure is indicative, keep the defect claim attached to the two witnesses and the control rather than to this probe, and register the schedule-dependence as the open question it is.

gaps.question: Does the natural rate of the term-regression interleaving rise with a delivery schedule that lands heartbeats more densely on election starts, or in configurations where an election's read-modify-write lasts longer, such as a multi-voter cluster or a slower stable store?

knowledge.statement: On one real single-node Raft instance with no instrumented store, 792 empty heartbeats were delivered on the fast path across about six seconds of alternating deposition and election starts, with a term sample taken immediately after each delivery: all 792 deliveries succeeded, no sampled term fell below the highest term already adopted, and the term ended at 2390 in memory and in the stable store with the node in Follower state. No natural fall was observed in 792 delivery opportunities under this schedule.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot 09193ea9b7ee4df99810e6eee7058028; single-voter node over the in-memory transport wrapped for the heartbeat fast path, plain in-memory store, deliveries in bursts of twelve every sixty milliseconds, each three terms above the node's current term, spaced about two milliseconds apart, sampled after each delivery; the schedule is bursty rather than uniformly distributed in time.

interpretations.joint_history: This probe belongs to the same investigation as the two witnesses and the control and uses the same setup with one deliberate difference: no instrumented store, so nothing holds the election's write open and the only question is whether the interleaving happens by itself. The three earlier receipts establish that the interleaving is possible, reproducible and attributable to the off-thread write; this one measures how often it showed up without help.
interpretations.rationale: The result is a negative and I am reading it as one: in 792 fast-path deliveries, all of which succeeded and each of which was followed immediately by a term sample, no sample fell below the highest term the node had already adopted, and the term ended at 2390 in memory and in the stable store. Since this implementation only ever writes a term as the current term plus one or as an adopted higher term, a fall would have been unambiguous, so the absence means the interleaving did not occur in this run rather than that it was missed by the sampler. The mechanism itself is unchanged and still rests on the two witnesses plus the control: the off-thread write can land between the election's read and its write and overwrite a higher term durably. What this run adds is a rate bound with its caveats named. With no falls in 792 delivery opportunities, a rule-of-three style bound puts the per-delivery probability below roughly a fraction of a percent, which is what one expects when the window is a couple of instructions wide and deliveries are spaced milliseconds apart; my deliveries were bursty rather than uniformly distributed in time, so the per-delivery figure is indicative of this schedule rather than a calibrated rate, and a schedule that lands heartbeats exactly on election starts, or a configuration where the election's read-modify-write lasts longer, could move it. I kept the defect claim where the evidence is - on the witnessed, reproduced and controlled regression - and did not upgrade this negative into either a refutation or a claim that the hazard is common.
counterevidence: Zero falls in 792 opportunities is consistent with a very small window and does not refute the mechanism; a negative of this kind cannot distinguish a rare interleaving from an unreachable one, which is why the claim rests on the witnesses and the control.

The deliveries were bursty rather than uniformly distributed, and each burst was aimed at the period after a deposition when an election is due, so the effective alignment with any given election start is unknown rather than measured.

The node was a single voter, so its elections resolve in one step; a multi-voter cluster or a slower persistent store would give the main loop a longer read-modify-write interval, which is the direction the open question points.
The probe exercises the wrapper transport that mirrors the network transport's dispatch rather than the network transport itself, so it bounds the rate for this delivery path.
limitations: Six seconds and 792 deliveries on one cluster shape: this bounds the rate for this schedule and says nothing about other schedules or configurations.
The per-delivery bound is derived from a rule-of-three style reading of zero events and should be treated as order-of-magnitude, not as a measured probability.
The single-voter configuration removes the peer traffic that a real deployment has, so both the opportunity structure and the aftermath differ from a cluster.

A denser delivery schedule is partly self-defeating as a way to raise the rate: every delivered heartbeat refreshes the follower's last contact and restarts the election timer it is trying to catch, so pushing harder postpones the campaign instead of landing more writes inside it; the direction the open question should take is therefore the one that lengthens the election's read-modify-write interval (a multi-voter cluster or a slower stable store) rather than the one that raises delivery density.
